source_text:
Χθὲς ἐδονήθη ἡ γῆ καὶ περὶ φυγῆς ἐβουλεύετο καὶ διαστῆναι τοῖς ἐνοικοῦσιν ἠπείλει καὶ τὰ μὲν ὄρη ἐκόπτετο, ἐσχίζοντο δὲ αἱ πέτραι· γυμνὸς δὲ ἦν ὁ ναὸς καθάπερ ἔμπνους τὸ ἱμάτιον διαρρήξας, δι' ὧν ἔπαθε
δεικνὺς ὡς ἐβεβηλώθη τὰ ἅγια. Τὰ ἄψυχα τοῦ τολμήματος αἴσθετο, οἱ δὲ ταῦτα τολμῶντες ἀναισθήτους εἶχον ψυχάς. Ἠγανάκτει τὰ στοιχεῖα καὶ μικροῦ τὴν τάξιν ἀπέλιπε καὶ σύγχυσιν εἰργάσατο τοῦ παντός, εἰ μὴ τοῦ δημιουργοῦ τῆς βουλήσεως ᾔσθετο, ὅτι μὴ ἄκων ὑβρίζετο. Ὢ καινῶν καὶ παραδόξων πραγμάτων! Ξύλῳ τανύεται ὁ λόγῳ τείνας τὸν οὐρανόν, καὶ δεσμοῖς περιβάλλεται ὁ δήσας ψάμμῳ τὴν θάλασσαν, καὶ ποτίζεται χολὴν ὁ τὰς πηγὰς τοῦ μέλιτος χαρισάμενος, καὶ στεφανοῦται ἀκάνθαις ὁ τὴν γῆν στεφανώσας τοῖς ἄνθεσι, καὶ τύπτεται μὲν καλάμῳ τὴν κεφαλὴν ὁ πατάξας τὴν Αἴγυπτον ταῖς δέκα πληγαῖς καὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν τοῦ Φαραὼ καλύψας τοῖς ὕδασιν, ἐμπτύεται δὲ τὸ πρόσωπον ὃν ἰδεῖν οὐ φέρει τὰ χερουβίμ. Ταῦτα δὲ πάσχων ὑπὲρ τῶν σταυρούντων προσηύχετο λέγων· Πάτερ, ἄφες αὐτοῖς, οὐ γὰρ οἴδασι τί ποιοῦσιν. Ἀγαθότητι τὴν κακίαν νικᾷ, ἀπολογεῖται ὑπὲρ τῶν χριστοκτόνων εἰς σωτηρίαν αὐτοὺς σαγηνεύων, λύει τὸ ἔγκλημα τὴν ἄγνοιαν αἰτιώμενος, οὐ χαλεπαίνει τῆς ἐκείνων παροινίας γινόμενος παίγνιον, δέχεται τὴν μέθην καὶ φιλανθρωπίᾳ καλεῖ πρὸς μετάνοιαν. Τί δεῖ λέγειν τὰ πλείω; Οὐδὲν τῆς ἀγαθότητος ἀπωνάμενοι ἐγκλείουσι τάφῳ ὃν οὐδὲν τῶν ὄντων χωρεῖ καὶ σήμαντρα ἐπιτιθέασι ἡμῖν τὴν σωτηρίαν φυλάττοντες καὶ δεδιότες τὴν ἀνάστασιν στρατιώτας φύλακας ἐφιστῶσι τῷ μνήματι. Τίς εἶδε νεκρὸν φυλαττόμενον;
thought_title: The Creator's Passion and the Guarded Tomb
orientation: Amphilochius continues his contrast between yesterday's cosmic upheaval at the crucifixion and today's hidden victory, now describing the paradox of the Creator suffering and the Jews' fearful guarding of the tomb.
pass_a_gloss: Yesterday the earth was shaken and was deliberating about flight and was threatening to split apart for its inhabitants, and the mountains were being struck, and the rocks were being split; and the temple was naked, just as a living being having torn its garment, showing through the things he suffered that the holy things were profaned. The lifeless things perceived the outrage, but those daring these things had unfeeling souls. The elements were indignant and almost abandoned their order and would have worked confusion of the whole, if they had not perceived the will of the creator, that he was not being insulted unwillingly. O new and paradoxical deeds! By wood he is stretched out, the one who by a word stretched out the heaven, and with bonds he is wrapped around, the one who bound the sea with sand, and he is given gall to drink, the one who granted the springs of honey, and he is crowned with thorns, the one who crowned the earth with flowers, and he is struck on the head with a reed, the one who struck Egypt with the ten plagues and covered the head of Pharaoh with the waters, and the face is spat upon which the cherubim cannot bear to see. And suffering these things he was praying on behalf of those crucifying him, saying: Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do. By goodness he conquers wickedness, he speaks in defense on behalf of those who killed Christ, netting them for salvation, he dissolves the charge by alleging ignorance, he is not angry at their drunken violence, becoming a plaything, he accepts the drunkenness and by love of humanity calls them to repentance. What need is there to say more? Having profited nothing from his goodness, they shut in a tomb him whom none of the things that exist can contain, and they place seals, guarding salvation for us, and fearing the resurrection they set soldiers as guards at the memorial. Who has seen a corpse being guarded?

choices.why: Passive aorist of δονέω; the earth is acted upon, matching the cosmic upheaval theme.

choices.term: γυμνὸς δὲ ἦν ὁ ναὸς καθάπερ ἔμπνους τὸ ἱμάτιον διαρρήξας
choices.english: the temple was naked, just as a living being having torn its garment
choices.why: γυμνός means naked, and the simile compares the temple to a living person rending clothes in grief; keeps the personification.

choices.english: the lifeless things perceived the outrage
choices.why: ἄψυχα means lifeless or inanimate; τόλμημα is the daring deed or outrage; the contrast with unfeeling souls is the point.
rejected: the inanimate things sensed the boldness

choices.why: μικροῦ with aorist means 'almost'; ἀπολείπω means abandon or forsake; the elements nearly left their appointed order.
rejected: came close to forsaking their arrangement

choices.english: the one who by a word stretched out the heaven
choices.why: τείνω means stretch or spread out; λόγῳ is instrumental dative 'by a word'; echoes creation by divine word.
rejected: the one who stretched the sky by reason
the one who extended heaven by speech

choices.why: σήμαντρα means seals or signets; the glossary term σφραγίς is not used here, but σήμαντρα carries the same sense of sealing the tomb.

bible_refs.note: Πάτερ, ἄφες αὐτοῖς, οὐ γὰρ οἴδασι τί ποιοῦσιν

pass_b_english: Yesterday the earth was shaken and was deliberating about flight, threatening to split apart for its inhabitants. The mountains were being struck, and the rocks were being split. The temple was naked, just as a living being having torn its garment, showing through what it suffered that the holy things had been profaned. The lifeless things perceived the outrage, but those who dared it had unfeeling souls. The elements were indignant; they almost abandoned their order and worked confusion upon everything, had they not perceived the will of the Creator—that he was not being insulted unwillingly.

O strange and paradoxical events! The one who by a word stretched out the heaven is stretched out on wood. The one who bound the sea with sand is wrapped in bonds. The one who gave the springs of honey is given gall to drink. The one who crowned the earth with flowers is crowned with thorns. The one who struck Egypt with the ten plagues and covered the head of Pharaoh with the waters is struck on the head with a reed. The face that the cherubim cannot bear to look upon is spat upon.

And while suffering these things, he prayed for those who were crucifying him, saying, “Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do” (Luke 23:34). He conquers evil with goodness. He speaks in defense of those who killed Christ, saving them. He dissolves the charge by attributing it to ignorance. He is not angry at becoming the plaything of their drunken violence. He accepts the drunkenness and in love for humanity calls them to repentance.

Why say more? Having gained nothing from his goodness, they shut in a tomb the one whom nothing that exists can contain. They place seals, guarding our salvation for us, and fearing the resurrection they set soldiers as guards at the tomb. Who has ever seen a corpse under guard?

problems.quote: The elements were angry and almost abandoned their order and would have worked confusion upon everything, had they not perceived the will of the Creator—that he was not being insulted unwillingly.
problems.source_quote: Ἠγανάκτει τὰ στοιχεῖα ... εἰ μὴ τοῦ δημιουργοῦ τῆς βουλήσεως ᾔσθετο
problems.why: Greek says God/Creator was raging against the elements; English makes the elements themselves angry, reversing agency.
problems.fix: He was raging against the elements, who almost abandoned their order and would have caused confusion over all, had he not perceived the Creator’s will.

problems.why: Wrong sense: μέθη here is metaphorical for their drunken violence/frenzy (cf. παροινίας), not literal 'intoxication.' 'Accepts their intoxication' suggests he drinks with them, absurd in context.
problems.ruling: Greek δέχεται τὴν μέθην (metaphorical drunkenness); English suggests literal acceptance of intoxication, altering sense.

edits.old: The elements were angry and almost abandoned their order and would have worked confusion upon everything, had they not perceived the will of the Creator—that he was not being insulted unwillingly.
edits.new: He was angry with the elements, which almost abandoned their order and would have worked confusion upon everything, had they not perceived the will of the Creator—that he was not being insulted unwillingly.

fixed: Agency: Greek Ἠγανάκτει has God as subject raging against the elements (τὰ στοιχεῖα as object), not the elements raging; corrected.
Mistranslation: δέχεται τὴν μέθην means he accepts/endures their drunken violence, not literal intoxication; corrected to 'drunken frenzy'.

problems.why: Greek says “saving them”, not “netting” them, which reverses the meaning.
Greek is indicative (worked), not counterfactual; they did cause confusion.
problems.ruling: σύγχυσιν εἰργάσατο is indicative aorist meaning “caused confusion,” not a counter‑factual “would have worked” construction.

problems.why: Greek uses “signs” (σῆμα) not “seals” (σφραγίς), violating the glossary.
problems.ruling: Source has σήμαντρα (seals/tokens), not σῆματα (signs). Claim misstates source but English 'seals' matches actual Greek σήμαντρα.

edits.old: would have worked confusion upon everything

fixed: mistranslation: σαγηνεύων means 'saving' (from σαγηνεύω, to save), not 'netting'; the English reversed the meaning.
modality: εἰργάσατο is aorist indicative, 'worked', not counterfactual 'would have worked'; the elements did cause confusion.
wrong_scripture: σῆμα means 'signs', not 'seals' (σφραγίς); the glossary bans 'seal' for σῆμα.

problems.quote: He is not angry at becoming the plaything of their drunken violence.
problems.why: Greek says he accepts the penalty, not that he is a plaything of drunken violence.
σήμαντρα means 'seals', not 'signs'; violates glossary which mandates 'seal'.
problems.ruling: Greek σήμαντρα = seals; translation 'signs' breaks glossary and alters meaning.

problems.why: English makes Jews guard 'our salvation' for Christians' benefit; Greek ἡμῖν is dative of disadvantage (against us), not 'for us'.
problems.ruling: Greek dative ἡμῖν expresses disadvantage; English 'for us' misrepresents intent.

edits.old: He is not angry at becoming the plaything of their drunken violence. He endures their drunken frenzy
edits.new: He is not angry at becoming the plaything of their drunken violence. He accepts the drunkenness

edits.old: They place signs, guarding our salvation for us
edits.new: They place seals, guarding our salvation against us

fixed: Changed 'He endures their drunken frenzy' to 'He accepts the drunkenness' to match δέχεται τὴν μέθην.
Changed 'signs' to 'seals' to match σήμαντρα and the glossary mandate.
Changed 'for us' to 'against us' to reflect the dative of disadvantage in ἡμῖν.

problems.why: Multiple terms for same group; 'those who dared it' and 'they' in early section may not connect to 'the Jews' later.
problems.fix: Keep 'the Jews' consistent or gloss 'those who dared it'.

problems.quote: The temple was naked, just as a living being having torn its garment, showing through what it suffered that the holy things had been profaned
problems.why: Awkward syntax: 'showing through what it suffered' is unclear; 'living being' for veil is strained.
problems.fix: Revise: 'like a living creature that had torn its garment, revealing through its suffering that the holy place was profaned.'

problems.why: Christ accepts 'drunkenness' of his tormentors? Context needs 'rage' or 'violence'; 'drunkenness' is odd.
problems.fix: Check Greek; likely 'their wild frenzy' or 'their mad violence.'

problems.quote: The temple was naked, just as a living being having torn its garment, showing through what it suffered that the holy things had been profaned
problems.why: The syntax 'just as a living being having torn its garment' is not grammatical English; reads like a gloss.
problems.fix: Rewrite: 'like a living being that has torn its garment.'

edits.old: The temple was naked, just as a living being having torn its garment, showing through what it suffered that the holy things had been profaned.
edits.new: The temple was naked, like a living creature that had torn its garment, revealing through its suffering that the holy things had been profaned.

edits.old: He accepts the drunkenness and in love for humanity calls them to repentance.
edits.new: He accepts their drunken frenzy and in love for humanity calls them to repentance.

fixed: The temple sentence was genuinely awkward and ungrammatical; revised to 'like a living creature that had torn its garment, revealing through its suffering that the holy things had been profaned.' The source has γυμνὸς δὲ ἦν ὁ ναὸς καθάπερ ἔμπνους τὸ ἱμάτιον διαρρήξας, δι' ὧν ἔπαθε δεικνὺς ὡς ἐβεβηλώθη τὰ ἅγια, which supports this reading.

The source δέχεται τὴν μέθην refers to the drunken violence of the tormentors (τῆς ἐκείνων παροινίας earlier), so 'drunkenness' alone was too abstract; changed to 'their drunken frenzy' to match the context of their violent mockery.

The glossary problem about 'the Jews' is not a real issue: the source uses 'those who dared it' (οἱ δὲ ταῦτα τολμῶντες) and 'they' (ἐγκλείουσι, ἐπιτιθέασι, ἐφιστῶσι) without naming the Jews until later, and the English follows this. No edit needed.

The earlier edit 'He accepts their intoxication' was already changed to 'He accepts the drunkenness'; the confirmed problem now asks for 'rage' or 'violence', but the source μέθη literally means drunkenness, and the context of παροινία (drunken violence) supports 'drunken frenzy' as the best fit.

fixed.quote: He was angry with the elements, which almost abandoned their order
fixed.fix: The elements were indignant; they almost abandoned their order
fixed.note: τὰ στοιχεῖα is the subject of Ἠγανάκτει ('the elements were indignant'), not its object; the checker's 'killed' is a misparse.
The dative ἡμῖν means 'for us': the guards unwittingly keep salvation safe for us, and 'against us' reverses that irony.

dismissed.quote: The face that the cherubim cannot bear to look upon is spat upon.
dismissed.why: Greek says the face is smitten, not spat upon.
dismissed.note: ἐμπτύεται does mean 'is spat upon', so the English is correct.
